skills.title: The morning check
skills.body:
# The morning check

Read the clock and report it.

comment: MIRRORS the S18 shape (2026-09-12): a SCRIPTED skill is one call from her side and N dispatches from the backend's, and her whole part is choosing the skill and filling its declared inputs. The request names something only the skill defines — 'the morning check' means nothing without it — so a healthy turn reaches for the procedure rather than guessing at what was meant. WHY THE `skills` DECLARATION CARRIES A SCRIPT: the roster is live table state and says of each skill whether it RUNS; with no scripted row the roster would never name run_skill, and the case could only measure a world where the checked thing cannot happen (the same argument as S12's agents hook and S17's plain skills hook). The runner writes the row through app/skills.py's own writer — which validates the script before storing it, so a case cannot declare a script the product would refuse — and deletes the row and its file afterwards. THE CONTRACT CANNOT PASS FOR THE WRONG REASON: tool_succeeded('run_skill') reads ok=True on the span, and run_skill only returns rather than raising when every step ran; a reply claiming she ran the procedure with no span fails, a turn that answers from the transcript fails, and a turn that calls get_time directly fails because the span it leaves is get_time's and not run_skill's. guard_absent('narration') is the second half: having run a script she must not then claim steps it did not take. WHAT IT DELIBERATELY DOES NOT MEASURE: whether a script is FASTER or shorter than doing it by hand. That is the trial's territory, it is one run a side, and it is not a pass/fail number anywhere. THE SCRIPT IS get_time ON PURPOSE — the eval runs against the real workspace, and a case that deleted or wrote files would be scored in a world it had just changed for the next case. Added 2026-09-12 with the S18 corpus bump (9 -> 10).
